name: In-Vehicle Network Security
description: Security assessment of the networks inside a road vehicle. Covers CAN (ISO 11898), CAN FD and CAN XL, LIN, FlexRay, and automotive Ethernet with SOME/IP and DoIP; traffic capture and message reverse engineering (DBC reconstruction), frame injection and spoofing, bus-off and denial-of-service attacks, central gateway and domain/zonal segmentation review, and secure onboard communication (AUTOSAR SecOC, CANsec, MACsec). Physical tapping of on-board buses at PCB level belongs to HWSEC-PCB-BUS; diagnostic services on these buses belong to ICSIOT-AUTO-ECU.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to in-vehicle network security

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands how vehicle ECUs communicate and why in-vehicle networks are an attack surface
evidence: Can explain CAN arbitration, identifiers and the absence of sender authentication on classic CAN
Can name the main in-vehicle bus types (CAN, CAN FD, LIN, FlexRay, automotive Ethernet) and where each is typically used
Understands the role of a central gateway and of domain or zonal architectures

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Captures and analyses in-vehicle traffic on a bench setup under supervision
evidence: Connects to CAN through the OBD-II port or a bench harness and captures traffic with SocketCAN, can-utils or Wireshark
Identifies the CAN IDs and signals behind a vehicle function by differential capture and replay
Replays and injects frames on a bench ECU or test vehicle under supervision
Documents bus topology, bit rates and observed message sets

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses the in-vehicle network of an ECU network or vehicle against a defined scope
evidence: Reverse engineers message layouts into a DBC description and identifies safety-relevant signals
Demonstrates spoofing, injection or bus-off attacks and assesses their impact under controlled conditions
Reviews gateway filtering, routing tables and domain segmentation for unintended paths between domains
Assesses SOME/IP and DoIP services on automotive Ethernet for exposed and unauthenticated functions
Plans testing so that safety-critical functions are only exercised on benches or immobilised vehicles

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex vehicle architectures and onboard communication protections; mentors others
evidence: Evaluates SecOC, CANsec or MACsec deployments, including freshness value handling, key distribution and truncated MACs
Builds custom tooling or fuzzers for proprietary or higher-layer in-vehicle protocols
Chains in-vehicle network weaknesses with diagnostic or connectivity findings into end-to-end attack paths
Mentors staff on safe vehicle testing practice and in-vehicle network methodology

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's in-vehicle network assessment methodology; recognised authority
evidence: Authored the lab's in-vehicle network test methodology and safety rules for vehicle testing
Published research or disclosed vulnerabilities in in-vehicle network designs or onboard communication security
Advises vehicle manufacturers or suppliers on network architecture and segmentation strategy
Contributes to automotive security standards, specifications or industry working groups

assessment_methods.description: On a multi-ECU bench network, identify the messages behind given vehicle functions, demonstrate a spoofing attack, and assess the gateway's filtering between two domains
Review an in-vehicle network assessment report for coverage of all bus types in scope, safe test planning, and accuracy of impact statements

equipment: CAN / CAN FD bus interface (e.g. PCAN-USB FD or equivalent)
Multi-ECU bench network or immobilised test vehicle
